newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Apple to cut 250 Singapore jobs, PCB output.
newsitem.headline: Apple to cut 250 Singapore jobs, PCB output.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc will cut 250 jobs in Singapore and halt production of printed circuit boards (PCBs) in the country, a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"We talked to staff on the manufacturing side. We told them the aim was to be a demand fulfilment centre for Asia-Pacific and Japan," said Sue Sara, corporate affairs manager for Apple Asia-Pacific.
The company intends to concentrate on systems assembly.
Sara said the Singapore plant would focus on all aspects of the supply chain, to meet domestic and export needs, but the production of PCBs would be farmed out to another company.
"We will announce our choice of vendor by the end of the month. Outsourcing will be by the end of August," Sara said.
She said the lay-offs were in addition to the 101 jobs the company shed in Singapore by shutting down a design centre seven weeks ago.
The latest cuts will reduce the Singapore workforce by about 28 percent to just over 600.
Apple said in March it would cut 4,100 jobs worldwide, or nearly a third of its workforce, and discontinue its consumer computer line to reduce costs and return to profits.
The company reported a second-quarter loss of US$708 million in April due to weaker sales of its personal computers.
